person_note: The quote set repeatedly exposes Louisa Clark as a participating “I” narrator across reflective, scenic, and dialogue-adjacent passages from the novel. Universal uses of “you” are maxims or self-directed generalizations, while quoted speech and isolated ambiguous fragments are local rather than competing narrative strands. Authorized Penguin opening extracts independently confirm first-person Louisa narration, and two explicit whole-book sources state that Still Me remains entirely in her first-person perspective. No credible evidence of sustained second- or third-person sections was found; the only limitation is that the Tier A excerpts cover the opening rather than the complete book.
